notes: parseProjectModuleFile (projectModuleParsing.ts:25) returns null (not a thrown ZodError) when a non-semantic module fails ModuleCartridgeSchema; the try/catch at lines 90-94 does not catch that, and line 95 `if (module)` silently drops it, so an invalid module is omitted from the returned map without error. Name promises rejection; code silently skips.

pending is keyed by nextFile, a project-relative filename (line 51), yet the loop binds it to a variable named `path`; writeModule's parameter is `filename` and resolves it via resolveProjectFile. Genuine name/reality mismatch but benign since the value is a valid relative filename and resolution is correct.

stageProjectVersion reads/mutates the module-level stagedVersions Map, and once an entry exists (lines 43-47) subsequent bumps recompute from staged.baseVersion, ignoring the passed-in currentManifestVersion. Signature reads pure but is stateful and drops the arg after the first call, as claimed.

ns.startsWith(oldNamespace) plus filename.replace(oldNamespace,...) (lines 40-41) and manifest file.replace (line 65) match by bare prefix, so renaming `foo` also moves/renames `foobar.json` to `Cbar.json` and rewrites sibling files. (replaceRefs uses `${from}::` so ref bodies are delimiter-safe, but the filename/manifest corruption is real.)

filename.replace (line 41) and file.replace (line 65) use single-match String.replace, while replaceRefs uses replaceAll (line 9). A filename or manifest entry containing the old namespace twice is only half-rewritten, diverging from the fully-rewritten refs; narrower but real.

stagedVersions is a module-level (process-global) Map cleared only by explicit clearStagedProjectVersion (line 55), so entries leak and are shared across all consumers on the same manifestPath. RefactorService.test.ts's beforeEach(clearStagedProjectVersion) confirms the cross-case statefulness is real.

Line 61 uses raw vfs.readFile ?? { files: [] }, and FileSystemBase.readFile returns null for string-stored values (base:57,66); on that path the empty fallback is written back at line 67, wiping name/version/files, whereas loadProject uses the object-or-text-aware readProjectManifest. Mechanism is code-confirmed; the wipe requires the manifest to be text-stored, which is a narrower path.

replaceRuntime seeds Runtime from Array.from(this.moduleCache.values())[0] (line 98), the first module by Map insertion order, not the linker's activeCartridge produced at loadProject:49. Which module runs depends on manifest.files ordering and the compiled cartridge is not what the runtime executes, as claimed.

Same defect as the guard at projectManifest.ts:95: parseProjectModuleFile returns null (projectModuleParsing.ts:25) for a non-semantic module failing ModuleCartridgeSchema, and `if (module)` drops it with no throw or log, so loadProject proceeds with an incomplete moduleCache. A malformed module silently vanishes.

Line 88 `if (!this.manifestPath || !root) return;` is a normal defensive early return when no project is loaded; there is nothing to reload, so the void return cannot produce wrong results. Technically silent but immaterial, as the finding itself concedes.

In reloadModules, line 90-91 reads each file and only sets the cache `if (mod)`; readFile returns null for missing or string-stored files (base:57,66), so such a file is silently skipped and the stale prior moduleCache entry is retained while the reload appears to succeed. Real silent skip, though impact is bounded since linkProject re-reads independently.
